content: Do not increase your dose or take this medication more frequently than prescribed without consulting your doctor. The maximum recommended dose is 5 milligrams within 24 hours, or 0.75 milligrams within 24 hours for certain formulations. Antacids can reduce the absorption of hyoscyamine, so avoid taking them simultaneously. Common side effects of hyoscyamine may include dizziness, drowsiness, blurred vision, dry mouth, headache, difficulty sleeping, constipation, flushing, dry skin, and reduced sweating. These effects are generally mild, but if they persist or worsen, contact your healthcare provider. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but can occur. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. In the United States, you can call your doctor for medical advice about side effects or contact the FDA. In Canada, consult your doctor or Health Canada for guidance. Before taking hyoscyamine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to atropine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Additionally, this medication may contain alcohol, so caution is advised if you have alcohol dependence or liver disease. Hyoscyamine may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or blurred vision. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness or clear vision until you are sure you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages while taking this medication. This drug may also increase the risk of heatstroke by reducing sweating, so take precautions in hot weather. Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medication, particularly confusion, drowsiness, unusual excitement, constipation, and difficulty urinating. During pregnancy, hyoscyamine should only be used when clearly needed, as it passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Check the labels on all your medications, such as allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. Hyoscyamine may interfere with certain lab tests, potentially causing false results. Inform laboratory personnel and your doctor that you are using this medication. In case of overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Managing digestive disorders may involve lifestyle changes such as stress reduction programs, regular exercise, smoking cessation, and dietary adjustments to enhance the effectiveness of this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for disposal instructions. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
